development-of-practical-skills: A newton, a joule, a watt: what are they actually made of?
foundations-of-physics: Roughly how many times does a heart beat in a lifetime: 10⁶, 10⁹ or 10¹²?
forces-motion: A runner finishes a lap exactly where she started. What was her average velocity?
electrons-waves-photons: Rub a balloon and it becomes charged. Where did that charge come from?
newtonian-world-astrophysics: In a cold room, metal feels colder than wood. Is it really at a lower temperature?
particles-medical-physics: A charged capacitor has no net charge at all. So what is it actually storing?
astrophysics-and-cosmology-part-1: A smudge of light in a telescope: how do astronomers work out what they are looking at?
astrophysics-and-cosmology-part-2: Two stars look equally bright in the night sky. How can we tell which one really gives out more light?
circular-motion: A car rounds a bend at a steady speed. Is it accelerating, and if so, how much?
electric-fields: Halve the distance between two charges. How many times bigger does the force between them get?
electrical-circuits: One dead bulb can put out a whole string of lights, yet home lamps work on their own. Why?
electromagnetism: Switch on a current in a wire just above a compass. Which way does the needle turn, and why?
energy-power-and-resistance: A battery is marked one and a half volts, a lamp six. What exactly does a volt count?
forces-in-action-part-1: With air resistance ignored, which forces still act on a ball once it has left your foot?
forces-in-action-part-2: Can an object's balance point be in empty space, where there is no material at all?
gravitational-fields: Astronauts float on the space station. How much weaker is Earth's gravity up there?
materials: Why are the markings on a spring weighing scale evenly spaced?
medical-imaging: How does slamming electrons into a lump of metal make X-rays?
newtons-laws-of-motion-and-momentum: When a truck hits a small car, which one feels the bigger force?
nuclear-and-particle-physics-part-1: Blow an atom up to the size of a stadium. How big is the nucleus at its heart?
nuclear-and-particle-physics-part-2: Protons and neutrons are built from the same two kinds of quark. Why is only one of them charged?
nuclear-and-particle-physics-part-3: A helium nucleus is lighter than the protons and neutrons that make it. Where did the missing mass go?
oscillations: Why does an oscillating mass on a spring move fastest at the one point where no overall force acts on it?
quantum-physics: Why can a few minutes of weak ultraviolet damage skin cells' DNA when hours of bright red light can't?
waves-part-1: Sing a higher note. Does the sound reach the far side of the room any sooner?
waves-part-2: Why does light bend as it enters water, but not when it hits the surface head-on?
waves-part-3: Two slits, a laser and a ruler: how can stripes on a wall measure a wavelength far thinner than a hair?
work-energy-and-power: Hold a heavy bag still for ten minutes and your arms ache. How much work have you done on the bag?
